'''Mina Aganagić''' is a [[mathematical physics|mathematical physicist]] who works as a professor at the [[Berkeley Center for Theoretical Physics|Center for Theoretical Physics]], the Department of Mathematics, and the Department of Physics at the [[University of California, Berkeley]].<ref>[https://physics.berkeley.edu/people/faculty/mina-aganagic profile at Physics Department, UC Berkeley]</ref><ref>[https://math.berkeley.edu/people/faculty/mina-aganagic profile at Math Department, UC Berkeley]</ref>

==Career==
Aganagić was raised in [[Sarajevo]], [[Socialist Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina|Bosnia and Herzegovina]], [[Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia|Yugoslavia]].<ref name="sloan" />
She has a bachelor's degree and a doctorate from the [[California Institute of Technology]], in 1995 and 1999 respectively; her PhD advisor was [[John Henry Schwarz]].<ref>{{mathgenealogy|id=162853}}</ref>  She was a [[postdoctoral researcher|postdoctoral fellow]] at the [[Harvard University]] physics department
from 1999 to 2003. She then joined the physics faculty at the [[University of Washington]], where she became a [[Sloan Research Fellowship|Sloan Research Fellow]]<ref name="sloan">{{citation|url=https://www.washington.edu/news/2004/03/11/three-profs-win-sloan-research-fellowships/|journal=UW Today|publisher=University of Washington|date=March 11, 2004|title=Three profs win Sloan Research Fellowships|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260317024110/https://www.washington.edu/news/2004/03/11/three-profs-win-sloan-research-fellowships/|archive-date=17 March 2026|url-status=live}}</ref> and a [[United States Department of Energy|DOE]] Outstanding Junior Investigator.<ref name="DOE">{{citation|url=https://science.energy.gov/~/media/hep/pdf/files/pdfs/OJI_ALL_Awards.pdf|title=US Department of Energy Outstanding Junior Investigator Awards|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150721035058/http://science.energy.gov/~/media/hep/pdf/files/pdfs/OJI_ALL_Awards.pdf|archive-date=21 July 2015|url-status=dead}}</ref> She moved to UC Berkeley in 2004. In 2016 the [[Simons Foundation]] gave her a Simons Investigator Award<ref>{{citation|url=https://www.ams.org/news?news_id=3115|title=Simons Investigator Awards Announced|work=News, Events and Announcements|publisher=[[American Mathematical Society]]|date=July 13, 2016|access-date=2017-09-20}}</ref> and the same year [[American Physical Society]] had awarded her with its fellowship.<ref>{{citation|url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/fellowships/archive-all.cfm?initial=&year=2016&unit_id=&institution=|title=APS Fellow Archive|publisher=American Physical Society|access-date=1 December 2019}}</ref><ref>{{citation |title=Mina Aganagic {{!}} Physics |url=https://physics.berkeley.edu/people/faculty/mina-aganagic |access-date=2026-08-26 |website=physics.berkeley.edu}|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260316060549/https://physics.berkeley.edu/people/faculty/mina-aganagic|archive-date=16 March 2026|url-status=live}}</ref>
